claim.quote: Observation of a neutrino burst in coincidence with supernova 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud

date.note: Publication date; the burst itself arrived on 23 February 1987 (APS news release).

key_value_text.quote: A burst of eight neutrino events preceding the optical detection of the supernova in the Large Magellanic cloud has been observed in a large underground water Cherenkov detector.
key_value_text.value: A burst of eight neutrino events with visible energies of 20-40 MeV spanning six seconds

name: Observation of a neutrino burst in coincidence with supernova 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud
notes: The IMB burst was found after Kamiokande announced its own 11 events (APS News); the two results are recorded as separate results of separate experiments.

summary.plain: The IMB tank in an Ohio salt mine recorded eight neutrinos in six seconds a few hours before the light from supernova 1987A reached Earth. Along with the Japanese Kamiokande detector, it gave the first direct measurement of neutrinos from a supernova.
summary.technical: A burst of eight neutrino events with visible energies of 20-40 MeV spanning 6 s, contained in the IMB water Cherenkov detector near the estimated time of core collapse, against a background of about 2 per day.

title: Observation of a neutrino burst in coincidence with supernova 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud
why_it_matters: APS: "this was the first time that neutrinos from a supernova were measured directly", and the measurements "became the starting point for the field of neutrino astronomy".
